body: Monday, February 14 2022 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information available before 2022-02-14 00:00 UTC. Prices use completed prior sessions. Prepared retrospectively; later outcomes are excluded.

Macro Stance: Two shocks now push US equity multiples in the same direction. January consumer prices rose 7.5% from a year earlier, the hottest reading since 1982 and more than expected, according to CNBC.  [1]  Bloomberg described the gain as larger than forecast.  [2]  On Friday the White House added that Russia could invade Ukraine within the week, Stars and Stripes reported.  [3]  The S&P 500 fell 1.90% to 4,418.64 index points and the Nasdaq 100 lost 3.07% to 14,253.84 index points, while the VIX jumped 3.45 points to 27.36 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). We are Bearish on duration-heavy US equity: the Fed is being pulled forward just as an exogenous risk premium is being added.

Rates & Curve: The two-year Treasury closed at 1.50% and the ten-year at 1.92%, leaving the 10Y−2Y spread at +42 bps on a positively sloped curve (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). Over 20 observations the two-year has risen 59 bps from 0.91% while the ten-year is up only 22 bps from 1.70%, so the spread has compressed by 37 bps: a bear flattening, with both yields up and the two-year up more. The last five observations concentrate the move, with the two-year up 19 bps and the ten-year down 1 bp, after the ten-year briefly topped 2% for the first time since 2019 on the inflation print, according to CNBC.  [4]  Reuters has published an explainer on why the flattening matters.  [5]  The front of the curve is still steep, with 10Y−3M at +156 bps, so the Fed has room to hike before inversion becomes the dominant signal.

New / Most Important: The policy debate has moved from whether to how fast. Reuters reports that hot inflation fuels the case for a 'big-bang' Fed hike in March.  [6]  Against that, the Fed's Barkin told Reuters he would have to be convinced of the need for a half-point move.  [7]  Households are already absorbing the shock: Yahoo Finance describes US consumers as 'in a deep funk'  [8] , and the Orange County Register reports the 30-year mortgage rate has surged to 3.69%, a two-year high.  [9]  The dollar index (DXY) rose 0.55% on Friday to 96.08 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), tightening financial conditions further. The geopolitical layer is the new element: a war premium is now competing with the Fed for the same drawdown budget.

Playbook ✓: Action: stay underweight the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ closed at 347.06 USD, down 8.10% over 20 sessions) against the energy sector ETF (XLE, up 11.71% over the same span), and hold seven-to-ten-year Treasuries (IEF, up 1.04% on Friday) as the war hedge rather than adding equity beta (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to press the trade: the VIX holding above 27.36 index points while the two-year stays at or above 1.50% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). What changes the call: a verifiable Russian pull-back that sends the VIX back toward its 20-session reference of 20.31 index points, combined with a softer next inflation print, would argue for covering growth underweights before the March meeting.

Macro Stance: Europe is where the Ukraine risk and the inflation problem meet, and the ECB is not yet offering a backstop. Reuters argues the ECB 'put' for euro zone bond markets is some way off.  [10]  Germany's Scholz has warned Moscow of immediate sanctions if Ukraine is attacked, per Reuters  [11] , and DW describes his diplomacy as a delicate mission.  [12]  We are Bearish on euro-area equities relative to the UK.

Activity & Inflation: Lagarde has said there is no need for big ECB tightening because inflation should settle at target, per Yahoo Finance UK  [13] , although Al Jazeera reports she is no longer ruling out a hike this year.  [14]  Price pressure is broadening: Eurostat flagged rising euro-area energy prices in 2021  [15] , Dutch inflation has reached its highest point in 40 years, per IamExpat  [16] , and UK motorists face record fuel prices, per the Guardian.  [17]  The Bank of England has hiked for a second time while the ECB stays put, per Barron's  [18] , and the ONS has published its first estimate of UK GDP for October to December.  [19]

New / Most Important: Dutch TTF gas, the key transmission channel, rose 4.13% on Friday to 77.43 EUR/MWh, though it is still 9.40% below its level 20 sessions earlier, while the STOXX 600 slipped 0.59% to 469.57 index points and the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 1.00% to 4,155.23 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The EIA notes Europe relies primarily on imports to meet its natural gas needs.  [20]  The UK is the relative refuge: the FTSE 100 held at 7,661.00 index points, down just 0.15% on the day and up 1.56% over 20 sessions, as BP rose 1.58% and Shell 1.02% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Playbook ✓: Action: prefer FTSE 100 exposure over the Euro Stoxx 50, whose US-listed ETF (FEZ) fell 2.71% on Friday, until gas risk is priced out (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to deepen the underweight: TTF reclaiming its 20-session reference of 85.46 EUR/MWh. What changes the call: an ECB signal that it would lean against spread widening, or a diplomatic de-escalation that pushes TTF lower while growth holds.

Macro Stance: China is the one major economy easing while the Fed tightens, and that divergence is the core of our Mixed stance. Bloomberg describes the PBOC as seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes  [21] , after it cut key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years, according to CNBC.  [22]  The easing is starting to show up in credit, but it has not yet repaired the property chain or the consumer, and exporters face a more hostile trade backdrop. Investors are being asked to trust a policy pivot before the activity data confirm it.

PMIs & Activity: The latest factory read was soft: the Caixin PMI showed January activity contracting as Covid lockdowns bit, per Reuters.  [23]  That follows a strong 2021 base, with GDP growth of 8.1%, the fastest in a decade, as Global Times reported  [24] , and fixed-asset investment up 4.9% in 2021, according to Macau Business.  [25]  China Daily reports industrial profits rebounded in 2021 as production improved.  [26]  Consumption is the weak leg: CNBC reports the holiday box office plunged 23% as theaters pushed prices to record highs.  [27]  On the supply side, Reuters says China plans to increase iron ore output and boost steel-scrap use  [28] , a sign Beijing wants to contain input costs for the infrastructure push that China Briefing describes as the growth lever for 2022.  [29]

Credit Impulse: The clearest early win for the easing camp is credit. Reuters reports Chinese government bond yields rose on faster January credit growth  [30] , which is the bond market saying it believes the impulse is turning. Lower policy rates reinforce that, with Fibre2Fashion noting cuts to medium-term lending and reverse repo rates.  [31]  The mechanism matters for global assets: a rising Chinese credit impulse tends to support Asian cyclicals and industrial commodities with a lag, but this cycle the property sector is where much of the new credit needs to land, and developers' capacity to absorb it is impaired.

Property: Property remains the drag that keeps us from turning Bullish. Reuters reports regulators are giving developers easier access to escrowed presale funds  [32] , a targeted liquidity release rather than a bailout. Evergrande says it aims to deliver 600,000 apartments in 2022 with no fire sales, per Reuters  [33] , while the WSJ reports its CEO sold bonds before the profit warning  [34] , a reminder that bondholder trust is broken. Nikkei Asia's reporting on concrete 'ghost towns' underlines the inventory overhang  [35] , and in Hong Kong lived-in home valuations are dropping amid a fifth Covid wave, per the South China Morning Post.  [36]  Business Recorder reported in January that new home prices fell less in December on promotions and easing curbs  [37] , so price stabilization is being bought with discounts. Escrow relief buys time; it does not create buyers.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Trade policy is turning more coercive in both directions. China suspended Lithuanian beef, dairy and beer imports as the Taiwan row grows, per Reuters  [38] , and Taiwan, Canada and Japan have asked to join the EU's WTO case against China, according to Politico Europe.  [39]  The Phase One relationship is souring too: the Peterson Institute calculates China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports in the Trump-era trade deal.  [40]  Domestically, oversight keeps tightening, with Reuters reporting a fine for Ant-backed MYBank over credit-scoring rules.  [41]  On Russia, The Hill argues China is making sanctions irrelevant  [42] , a stance that could raise secondary-sanctions risk for Chinese banks and exporters.

Markets & Flows: Onshore and offshore markets are telling different stories. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,462.95 index points, down 0.66% on Friday and up 3.02% over five sessions, a window that reaches back before the Lunar New Year closure, but still 3.26% lower over 20 sessions; the Hang Seng finished at 24,906.66 index points, 4.92% higher over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). In New York the China A-shares ETF (ASHR) fell 1.93% and the China internet ETF (KWEB) 3.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Regulatory risk remains sharp and idiosyncratic: WuXi Biologics sank by a record after landing on a US red-flag list, per the SCMP.  [43]  The SCMP's Macroscope column argues emerging markets are the ones to watch as tech-led US stocks lose their shine.  [44]

New / Most Important: Technology self-sufficiency is the most important new strand. China's biggest chipmaker SMIC posted record revenue despite US sanctions, per CNBC  [45] , and plans to boost capacity after doubling profits to US$1.7 billion, according to the SCMP.  [46]  At the same time ASML has flagged possible IP infringement by a Chinese 'little giant', per the SCMP  [47] , which the Chinese company denies, according to Reuters.  [48]  Nikkei Asia reports ZTE is boosting its chip capabilities amid Huawei's crackdown woes.  [49]  Foreign capital is still committing to the premium consumer: BMW paid $4.2 billion to take control of its Chinese joint venture, Reuters reports.  [50]  Capital is flowing toward strategic self-sufficiency and premium consumption rather than the old property-led model.

Playbook ✓: Action: keep China at neutral, expressed through Hong Kong-listed platforms such as Tencent (453.04 HKD, up 6.84% over 20 sessions) rather than the A-share ETF (ASHR, down 4.07% over 20 sessions) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to upgrade: a second month of accelerating credit growth alongside a factory PMI back in expansion. What changes the call: new US listing or sanctions actions against Chinese firms, or an escrow scheme that fails to stop developer defaults. ⚠ Divergence: bond yields are rising on faster credit growth, which normally signals reflation, yet the Caixin factory gauge is contracting and holiday spending is weak; the credit impulse has not yet reached activity.

Macro Stance: Japan is the least exposed major market to the Fed shock through policy, and among the most exposed through industry. The BOJ still applies a negative rate to some bank deposits, including MUFG Bank's, per the Asahi Shimbun  [51] , and Reuters reported in January that it was debating how to message an eventual rate hike as inflation perks up.  [52]  Tokyo was shut for a holiday on Friday, so the Nikkei 225's last close of 27,696.08 index points, up 0.42%, predates the US risk-off (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). We are Mixed: policy is a cushion, but the export sector is chip-constrained.

Activity & Currency: The industrial picture is a chip story. Toyota's profits fell as production was hit, per the BBC  [53] , and the Japan Times argues that after a tough 2021 the outlook for Japanese carmakers is now down to chips.  [54]  Nissan raised its profit outlook but sees chips limiting growth, according to Reuters.  [55]  Demand is not the constraint: Reuters reported in January that December exports and imports hit record highs by value as supply bottlenecks eased.  [56]  Toyota closed at 2,254.00 JPY, down 6.55% over 20 sessions, while chip-equipment makers Tokyo Electron (57,150.00 JPY) and Advantest (9,600.00 JPY) rose 1.82% and 2.78% in their last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). On the currency, the mechanics favor the dollar: with the US two-year at 1.50% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11) and Japanese wages not rising, as the Japan Times explains  [57] , rate differentials keep widening, and the DXY is 1.36% firmer over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Playbook ✓: Action: underweight Japanese chip-equipment names into the reopening, because the US-listed Japan ETF (EWJ) fell 0.81% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 4.83% in a session Tokyo missed (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger: Tokyo Electron failing to hold its last-session gain would confirm the catch-down. What changes the call: evidence that chip supply is easing for carmakers, or a BOJ signal of normalization that would remove the rate-differential tailwind for exporters.

Macro Stance: Australia combines strong domestic data with a central bank that wants more proof before hiking. The SMH reports Australia is ending QE with a murky future for $650b of assets  [58] , following the RBA's February policy statement.  [59]  Inflation hit 3.5%, per the AFR  [60] , and the jobless rate is at a 13-year low, per The Australian.  [61]  We are Mixed: the data argue for hikes sooner than the RBA signals.

Demand & Financing: Credit demand is still driven by housing. CBA reported a first-half profit surge on the home boom and unveiled a share buyback, per Reuters  [62] , and The Australian says the bank is bullish on the economy as rate hikes loom.  [63]  The AFR flags rising rents as a sleeper factor for inflation  [64] , and the reopening of borders to vaccinated tourists on February 21 adds a services impulse, per Al Jazeera.  [65]  Supply remains a bottleneck, with Al Jazeera also reporting that border limbo in the mining state is sparking production fears.  [66]  Markets were softer on Friday: the S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.98% to 7,217.30 index points and CBA lost 2.21% to 98.55 AUD, while CSL is down 11.79% over 20 sessions and BHP gained 1.20% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Playbook ✓: Action: prefer the iron ore miners, with Fortescue up 6.98% over five sessions and Rio Tinto up 2.86% on Friday, over the banks while the RBA keeps its patient line (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger: a hawkish shift in RBA language after the next wage or inflation print. What changes the call: China's plan to raise domestic iron ore output, reported by Reuters  [28] , turning into weaker seaborne demand, or a faster RBA pivot that slows bank loan growth.

Macro Stance: Poland combines the most hawkish central bank in our coverage with the most direct exposure to the Russia–Ukraine risk, which is why we are Mixed rather than outright Bearish. The Monetary Policy Council (RPP) raised rates again, taking them to their highest level in almost nine years, according to Rzeczpospolita.  [67]  NBP Governor Adam Glapiński framed his press conference around being a hawk ('Ja jako jastrząb', or 'Me as a hawk'), Interia reported  [68] , and Bankier credited him with strengthening the zloty  [69] , which it later described as the strongest in eight months.  [70]  The inflation problem behind that stance is real: GUS put end-2021 inflation at 8.6%, per 300Gospodarka  [71] , and Credit Agricole has raised its 2022 forecast to 7.5%, per Bankier.  [72]  The labour market keeps the pressure on, with average pay up 9.6% in 2021, per pb.pl  [73] , and registered unemployment at 5.6% in January, per Radio Maryja citing the family and social policy ministry (MRiPS).  [74]

Markets: Warsaw has lagged the hawkish story. The iShares MSCI Poland ETF (EPOL) fell 3.88% on Friday to 20.31 USD and is down 10.96% over 20 sessions, while the WIG20 total-return tracker lost only 0.55% to 37.94 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The gap reflects mechanics: EPOL trades in dollars during New York hours, so it absorbs both currency translation and late-session US news, whereas the Warsaw close comes earlier in the day. Banks, the natural beneficiaries of higher rates, were heavy: Bank Pekao fell 2.24% to 133.15 PLN and PKO Bank Polski 1.04% to 47.65 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Parkiet still argues bank shares on the GPW have the potential to extend their bull run  [75] , while Bankier asks whether the market is still in a correction or already in a bear market.  [76]

Fiscal & Politics: Fiscal numbers are better than feared, but the politics are messier. The finance ministry estimates the 2021 state budget deficit at 26.3 bn zł, per Bankier  [77] , and Rzeczpospolita argues inflation is helping the government manage the public debt.  [78]  The Polski Ład tax reform has become a liability: deputy finance minister Jan Sarnowski, who was responsible for it, has lost his post, according to Business Insider Polska  [79] , a dismissal PolsatNews ties to the problems with Polski Ład  [80] , and Wyborcza.biz reports the next finance minister will be a woman.  [81]  Spending pressure is building, with pension indexation set to cost more than the budget assumed because of a higher index, per 300Gospodarka.  [82]  The food VAT cut is a double-edged tool that Credit Agricole says will contribute to higher inflation, per Bankier.  [83]  Relations with Brussels remain strained, with the EU set to withhold funds over the coal mine dispute, per DW.  [84]

Corporate & Sectors: Corporate news is dominated by energy security and state champions. Orlen's CEO says jobs at Lotos will be maintained, per Bankier  [85] , and INNPoland reports Orlen has raised its wholesale petrol price, with stations unwilling to absorb the increase.  [86]  KGHM has registered its copper cathodes on China's INE exchange, according to Inwestycje.pl  [87] , and Parkiet reports Jacek Sasin and KGHM are travelling to the US in pursuit of small nuclear reactors.  [88]  Utilities are positioning for transition and rates: netka.gda.pl reports PGE's Baltica 3 offshore wind farm, of about 1045 MW, is planned to start in 2026  [89] , and WNP.PL reports Tauron bought CO2 allowances at 30 euro and locked in a fixed interest rate.  [90]  In consumer names, LPP is optimistic about the year but expects cost pressure to weigh on margins, per Bankier.  [91]  Prices show the split: the coking-coal miner JSW is up 20.74% over 20 sessions and KGHM 9.44% over five, while Dino Polska is down 20.29% and Allegro 18.62% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Geopolitics & Security: Poland is now the staging ground for NATO reinforcement. Reuters reported exclusively that the US will send 3,000 additional troops to Poland  [92] , with ABC News reporting the 82nd Airborne deployment amid invasion concerns  [93] , and Politico Europe reports the UK is sending 350 more troops to the Polish border.  [94]  TVN24 describes further military transports arriving as proof that threats are being taken seriously  [95] , and Prime Minister Morawiecki has praised the UK's solidarity with Ukraine, Poland and NATO's eastern flank, per gov.pl.  [96]  Defence24 reports that Polish-made Piorun MANPADS have been exported to the US and provided to Ukraine, a commercial success for Mesko.  [97]  Energy is the economic channel: Money.pl reports businesses have received letters warning of gas-supply restrictions  [98] , and a survey reported by Bankier finds Europeans fear Russia will attack Ukraine this year.  [99]

New / Most Important: The most important new signal is the NBP's reserve strategy. Business Insider Polska reports Glapiński intends to buy another 100 tonnes of gold  [100] , and Obserwator Gospodarczy calculates Poland could hold larger gold reserves than the UK or Saudi Arabia within a year.  [101]  Combined with Glapiński's pledge to keep urging tighter monetary policy, reported by PolsatNews  [102] , the message is that the NBP is building a war chest and is prepared to defend real rates and the currency. The Stowarzyszenie Inwestorów Indywidualnych reads the latest hike as a sign the NBP has not yet said its last word.  [103]  For markets, that lowers the probability of a disorderly currency sell-off even if the security situation deteriorates.

Playbook ✓: Action: hold Polish banks, PKO Bank Polski and Bank Pekao, as the rate-sensitive expression, fund them by underweighting the broad EPOL ETF until the Ukraine risk clears, and use JSW and KGHM as the commodity hedge. Trigger to add: another RPP hike with the currency's strength intact and EPOL stabilizing above its Friday close of 20.31 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). What changes the call: a Russian invasion that forces a flight from frontline assets, or fiscal slippage as Polski Ład repairs and pension costs pile up. ⚠ Divergence: the NBP is hawkish and Bankier reported the zloty at its strongest in eight months  [70] , which should support local assets, yet EPOL is down 10.96% over 20 sessions and bank shares sold off on Friday; the currency and the equity market are pricing different risks.

Narrative: Technology is where the bear flattening bites hardest, because long-dated cash flows are now discounted off a rising front end. XLK fell 3.05% on Friday to 154.89 USD and is down 5.77% over 20 sessions, with Adobe off 4.25% and Salesforce 4.49% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Reported: Fundamentals are not the problem. Tom's Hardware reports AMD set an all-time CPU market-share record  [104] , and the WSJ says Microsoft is keeping its finance head count flat with AI and bots.  [105]  The market is simply paying less for the same growth.

EPS Upside Watch: Consolidation is the upside lever. The WSJ reports Cisco made a takeover offer of more than $20 billion for Splunk  [106] , and Bloomberg says Microsoft is considering a deal for Mandiant.  [107]  Cash-rich acquirers can buy growth at compressed multiples, which favors large platforms over unprofitable software.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Apple's new way to pay by tapping iPhones together, per CNBC  [108] , shows the platforms moving into payments just as fintech multiples compress; Apple has held up better than peers, down 2.06% over 20 sessions to 168.64 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Narrative: Communication services has become the market's referendum on digital advertising. XLC fell 2.16% to 69.31 USD and is down 9.05% over 20 sessions, with Meta Platforms (FB) down 32.75% and Netflix 24.63% over the same span, and Alphabet fell 3.13% on Friday to 2,685.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Reported: Meta's fourth-quarter release triggered a sharp leg of the slide, with CNET reporting the shares plummeted on disappointing earnings and a user drop.  [109]  Disney is the counterexample: Variety reports Disney Plus ended 2021 with nearly 130 million subscribers, smashing growth forecasts  [110] , and Walt Disney is up 5.25% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

EPS Upside Watch: Capital return is the near-term lever: Twitter swung to a gain after announcing a new $4 billion buyback despite underwhelming user growth, per MarketWatch.  [111]  The Discovery–WarnerMedia deal has cleared US antitrust review, Reuters reports  [112] , setting up cost synergies for the combined streamer.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Forbes puts the impact of Apple's privacy changes on Meta at $10 billion  [113] , a reminder that platform rules, more than the ad cycle, now set earnings power in this sector.

Narrative: Financials should benefit from higher rates, but a flattening curve and a risk-off tape cap the upside. XLF fell 1.40% to 40.11 USD; JPMorgan Chase is down 8.51% and Goldman Sachs 7.10% over 20 sessions while Wells Fargo is up 4.13%, and the regional bank ETF (KRE) is down 4.99% as Charles Schwab fell 4.03% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Reported: Alternative managers are delivering: Forbes reports a record-breaking year at Apollo  [114] , and the WSJ says KKR's earnings fell while cash available to shareholders hit new heights.  [115]

EPS Upside Watch: Net interest margin is the swing factor. A Kansas City Fed study examines whether margins at small and large banks respond differently to rates  [116] ; with the two-year up 59 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11), asset-sensitive lenders should see the first lift.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Sanctions are a hidden cost: Global Trade Review warns banks face a compliance 'nightmare' over looming Russia sanctions  [117] . Meanwhile American Express is launching its first digital checking account, per CNBC  [118] , pushing a card network onto deposit turf.

Narrative: Energy is the market's cleanest hedge against both inflation and war. Brent rose 3.31% to 94.44 USD/bbl and WTI 3.58% to 93.10 USD/bbl, and XLE gained 2.91% to 70.41 USD, up 11.71% over 20 sessions, while Shell is up 12.00% over 20 sessions at 2,039.00 GBp (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Reported: Profits validate the move: Reuters says energy prices lifted BP's profits to an eight-year high  [119] , and the Borneo Bulletin reports TotalEnergies has returned to profit.  [120]  Equinor has published its fourth-quarter and year-end results.  [121]  Occidental Petroleum is up 25.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

EPS Upside Watch: The IEA has published its February Oil Market Report  [122] , and Reuters commentary calls diesel the US economy's inflation canary.  [123]  If middle distillates stay tight, refining margins benefit alongside upstream cash flow.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Shorts are leaning against the rally, per Barron's list of seven energy stocks with bearish bets  [124] , while AskTraders notes XLE has surged 23.2% in 2022.  [125]  Crowded skepticism into a war premium is fuel rather than friction; the bigger risk is the windfall-tax debate the BBC explains.  [126]

Narrative: Industrials have split into defense winners and cyclical losers. XLI fell 1.53% to 99.36 USD and is down 6.70% over 20 sessions, yet Lockheed Martin is up 8.49% over that span and Northrop Grumman rose 4.53% on Friday, while Caterpillar is down 11.35% and Eaton 11.99% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Reported: Maersk reported record earnings for 2021 with profit up triple, per the Indonesia Shipping Gazette  [127] , while Reuters says Boeing deliveries remain low as 787 problems weigh.  [128]

EPS Upside Watch: Defense primes face scrutiny as well as demand: Reuters reports Raytheon Technologies (RTX) says it is a 'target' of a DOJ probe into industry hiring practices. [259]  CNBC asks whether the deal was doomed from the start.  [260]  Without the deal, Nvidia trades on its core growth multiple just as the front end reprices.

Catalyst & Thesis: Food Business News reports Coca-Cola is beginning to hit pre-pandemic volume levels  [261] , and CNBC says its earnings beat estimates.  [139]  But RTE reports both PepsiCo and Coke warned of the inflation impact  [262] , so the margin path depends on price acceptance.

Price Hurdle & Risk: Coca-Cola closed at 60.29 USD, down 1.78% on Friday and 1.00% below its 20-session reference of 60.90 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The risk is that a second round of price increases dents volumes.

Trade Expression: Hold at market weight within staples; upgrade if it reclaims 60.90 USD while the VIX stays above 27.36 index points, confirming defensive sponsorship, and downgrade if PepsiCo, at 168.58 USD, keeps outperforming on pricing (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Monday's crowd story is the Crypto Bowl, an industry buying America's biggest broadcast to recruit first-time buyers, a customer-acquisition binge WIRED likens to Pets.com  [207] , while invasion fears send hedgers into gold miners.

Why Retail Is Here: The story the crowd tells itself is simple: when crypto is selling itself during the Super Bowl, the asset class has gone mainstream, and the only mistake is being late. Crypto companies are spending millions to win over viewers, CBS reported  [206] , and the New York Times told readers to prepare for this weekend's Crypto Bowl  [263] . The Washington Post profiled a 29-year-old CEO pushing crypto during the Super Bowl by giving away millions in bitcoin  [264] , and Marketplace framed the game as the marriage of crypto and sports  [265] . The hook is legitimacy by airtime plus free money. The price anchor flatters the pitch: bitcoin closed at 42,197.52 USD, up 15.12% over 20 sessions from 36,654.33 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13).

What Is Driving It: The blitz is booked into a rebound that has already stalled: bitcoin and ether dipped as US inflation numbers dented the wider crypto market recovery again, Gadgets 360 reported  [202] . Bitcoin slipped 0.11% on Sunday and is down 4.35% over five sessions, with ether off 7.66% to 2,883.46 USD and Solana 17.92% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13). The listed proxies took Friday's risk-off harder: Coinbase Global fell 5.00% to 194.53 USD and MicroStrategy 4.74% to 411.01 USD as the Nasdaq 100 lost 3.07% and the VIX jumped 14.43% to 27.36 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

The Social Signal: The attention evidence is about distribution more than chat-room volume. Terra signed a five-year, $40M sponsorship with the Washington Nationals  [266] ; Betterment is entering crypto through its Makara acquisition  [267] , which puts coins on a robo-adviser menu. The speculative fringe is warm as well: the Motley Fool is running if-you-had-invested-$100 stories on Shiba Inu  [268] , dogecoin added 3.15% on Sunday (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13), a CryptoPunks NFT sold for nearly $24M, doubling the previous record  [269] , and Reese Witherspoon has been touting NFTs on Twitter  [270] . When celebrities, ballparks and robo-advisers all point one way, the buyer being courted is the newcomer.

Historical Analog: WIRED's comparison is Pets.com  [207] , and the mechanism matters more than the brand: when an industry pours money into one mass-audience broadcast, it is admitting that its next leg of growth depends on people who have not bought yet. That is late-cycle customer acquisition, and it works only while prices reward the first purchase: a newcomer who buys after a 15.12% 20-session rebound and watches it fade becomes a seller, not a recruiter. Yahoo Finance's revival of the weird correlation between the Super Bowl and the stock market  [271]  treats the game itself as the signal. The ad slate is the better one, because heavy marketing at a peak of attention measures confidence among sellers, not durable demand among buyers.

Smart Money View: The professional split is real. Value investor Bill Miller says bitcoin miners are trading at very attractive valuations  [272] , Michael Saylor lays out why bitcoin beats property as a store of value  [273] , and Reuters reports Intel has launched a blockchain chip to tap the crypto boom  [179] . Against that, the plumbing looks fragile: Coinbase removed cryptocurrency links after rug-pull warnings  [205] , and another $10M was lost in a DeFi hack of Binance-listed Dego Finance  [274] . Regulators are circling the collectibles end of the pitch too: The Art Newspaper reports a US Treasury study finding the NFT market vulnerable to money laundering  [275] .

When the Narrative Breaks: The first test is conversion: airtime that does not turn into new accounts leaves the ad blitz looking like an acquisition bill paid near a local high. Price is the cleaner signal: a slide back toward the 20-session reference of 36,654.33 USD would erase the entire rebound the commercials are selling, and ether, the higher-beta coin, is already giving the faster warning (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-13). Macro supplies the trigger: the 10-year Treasury yield topped 2% for the first time since 2019 after the hot inflation print  [4]  before closing at 1.92% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11); a second break above 2% would reprice every liquidity-fed asset at once, and crypto has no earnings to cushion it. War is the calendar risk: the Biden–Putin call yielded no breakthrough, Al Jazeera reported  [235] , and weekend headlines hit crypto first because it is the only market open.

Why Retail Is Here: The war hedge is the most intuitive trade on the board: if Washington is pulling people out, own what rises on fear, with operating leverage. Biden told US citizens to leave Ukraine  [276] , the US ordered most embassy staff out  [277] , and gold jumped as rising Ukraine tensions spurred safe-haven demand  [197] . Gold futures closed at 1,842.10 USD/oz, up 0.26%, but the miners did the shouting: GDX rose 5.67% to 32.43 USD and Northrop Grumman 4.53% to 399.32 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The weekend added fuel, not relief: Biden told Putin an invasion would bring a decisive response, Reuters reported  [278] , and the talks yielded no breakthrough  [235] .

Where It Breaks: Miners amplify a headline premium and give it back fastest if diplomacy buys time; The Economist reports that a beleaguered Olaf Scholz has launched a diplomatic offensive  [279] , and any opening for talks would drain the bid. The underlying move is thin: gold is up 1.14% over 20 sessions from 1,821.40 USD/oz, and the 10Y Treasury yield at 1.92% is the hurdle a non-yielding hedge must beat (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). A GDX close back below 31.24 USD, its 20-session reference, would mark the war premium as spent (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).

Why Retail Is Here: The meme faithful are telling themselves their oldest story: when the market panics, the squeeze stocks are where the shorts get punished. AMC rose 22.54% over five sessions to 18.81 USD and GameStop 21.41% to 124.25 USD, and both gained on Friday while the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.07% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). AMC keeps feeding the believers, hiring a former Frito-Lay executive into a new growth role starting with popcorn  [280] , while the New York Times asks whether activist short sellers are misunderstood  [281] , a reminder the enemy is still there.

Where It Breaks: The rally lacks its old engine: Robinhood Markets fell 12.25% over five sessions to 13.32 USD while AMC and GameStop rose (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), and WIRED says the app's psych experiment backfired horribly  [282] . A squeeze needs new buyers through that door. AMC is still 8.95% below its 20-session reference of 20.66 USD; fading before reclaiming it would mark a relief pop, not a new leg.

Why Retail Is Here: Affirm is the purest buy-the-dip test on the board. The stock fell 20.67% on Friday to 46.55 USD, 25.82% over five sessions and 35.46% over 20 sessions from 72.13 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), after results that PYMNTS says shine a light on merchant take-rate tradeoffs  [184] . The bull case is Modern Retail's read that revenue growth is being driven by Amazon and Shopify  [283] . MarketWatch's question about 15 pandemic stocks that rose 100% or more and have since been crushed, asking whether it is now time to buy  [284] , is exactly the itch being scratched.

Where It Breaks: Affirm lends into a bear-flattening curve, with the 2Y yield up 59 bps over 20 observations to 1.50% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11), which tends to raise funding costs for a lender. Banking Day says the Zebit exit highlights the challenges for a profitless BNPL sector  [285] , and peers offer no cover: PayPal is down 36.31% over 20 sessions and Upstart fell 5.64% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). A close below Friday's 46.55 USD would turn the dip into a de-rating; the bull case needs stable take rates, not just a cheaper price.

geo.label: March lift-off, front end reprices
parts: Macro Stance

Two shocks now push US equity multiples in the same direction. January consumer prices rose 7.5% from a year earlier, the hottest reading since 1982 and more than expected, according to CNBC. [[n2132]] Bloomberg described the gain as larger than forecast. [[n2138]] On Friday the White House added that Russia could invade Ukraine within the week, Stars and Stripes reported. [[n1578]] The S&P 500 fell 1.90% to 4,418.64 index points and the Nasdaq 100 lost 3.07% to 14,253.84 index points, while the VIX jumped 3.45 points to 27.36 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). We are Bearish on duration-heavy US equity: the Fed is being pulled forward just as an exogenous risk premium is being added.
Rates & Curve

The two-year Treasury closed at 1.50% and the ten-year at 1.92%, leaving the 10Y−2Y spread at +42 bps on a positively sloped curve (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). Over 20 observations the two-year has risen 59 bps from 0.91% while the ten-year is up only 22 bps from 1.70%, so the spread has compressed by 37 bps: a bear flattening, with both yields up and the two-year up more. The last five observations concentrate the move, with the two-year up 19 bps and the ten-year down 1 bp, after the ten-year briefly topped 2% for the first time since 2019 on the inflation print, according to CNBC. [[n2192]] Reuters has published an explainer on why the flattening matters. [[n2198]] The front of the curve is still steep, with 10Y−3M at +156 bps, so the Fed has room to hike before inversion becomes the dominant signal.
New / Most Important

The policy debate has moved from whether to how fast. Reuters reports that hot inflation fuels the case for a 'big-bang' Fed hike in March. [[n2201]] Against that, the Fed's Barkin told Reuters he would have to be convinced of the need for a half-point move. [[n1365]] Households are already absorbing the shock: Yahoo Finance describes US consumers as 'in a deep funk' [[n2147]], and the Orange County Register reports the 30-year mortgage rate has surged to 3.69%, a two-year high. [[n2135]] The dollar index (DXY) rose 0.55% on Friday to 96.08 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11), tightening financial conditions further. The geopolitical layer is the new element: a war premium is now competing with the Fed for the same drawdown budget.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ closed at 347.06 USD, down 8.10% over 20 sessions) against the energy sector ETF (XLE, up 11.71% over the same span), and hold seven-to-ten-year Treasuries (IEF, up 1.04% on Friday) as the war hedge rather than adding equity beta (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to press the trade: the VIX holding above 27.36 index points while the two-year stays at or above 1.50% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11). What changes the call: a verifiable Russian pull-back that sends the VIX back toward its 20-session reference of 20.31 index points, combined with a softer next inflation print, would argue for covering growth underweights before the March meeting.

geo.label: ECB patient as energy risk rises
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is where the Ukraine risk and the inflation problem meet, and the ECB is not yet offering a backstop. Reuters argues the ECB 'put' for euro zone bond markets is some way off. [[n1306]] Germany's Scholz has warned Moscow of immediate sanctions if Ukraine is attacked, per Reuters [[n1499]], and DW describes his diplomacy as a delicate mission. [[n1342]] We are Bearish on euro-area equities relative to the UK.
Activity & Inflation

Lagarde has said there is no need for big ECB tightening because inflation should settle at target, per Yahoo Finance UK [[n1260]], although Al Jazeera reports she is no longer ruling out a hike this year. [[n1236]] Price pressure is broadening: Eurostat flagged rising euro-area energy prices in 2021 [[n1305]], Dutch inflation has reached its highest point in 40 years, per IamExpat [[n1309]], and UK motorists face record fuel prices, per the Guardian. [[n1996]] The Bank of England has hiked for a second time while the ECB stays put, per Barron's [[n1232]], and the ONS has published its first estimate of UK GDP for October to December. [[n1542]]
New / Most Important

Dutch TTF gas, the key transmission channel, rose 4.13% on Friday to 77.43 EUR/MWh, though it is still 9.40% below its level 20 sessions earlier, while the STOXX 600 slipped 0.59% to 469.57 index points and the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 1.00% to 4,155.23 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The EIA notes Europe relies primarily on imports to meet its natural gas needs. [[n1986]] The UK is the relative refuge: the FTSE 100 held at 7,661.00 index points, down just 0.15% on the day and up 1.56% over 20 sessions, as BP rose 1.58% and Shell 1.02% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer FTSE 100 exposure over the Euro Stoxx 50, whose US-listed ETF (FEZ) fell 2.71% on Friday, until gas risk is priced out (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to deepen the underweight: TTF reclaiming its 20-session reference of 85.46 EUR/MWh. What changes the call: an ECB signal that it would lean against spread widening, or a diplomatic de-escalation that pushes TTF lower while growth holds.

geo.label: Easing into a property drag
parts: Macro Stance

China is the one major economy easing while the Fed tightens, and that divergence is the core of our Mixed stance. Bloomberg describes the PBOC as seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0141]], after it cut key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years, according to CNBC. [[n0136]] The easing is starting to show up in credit, but it has not yet repaired the property chain or the consumer, and exporters face a more hostile trade backdrop. Investors are being asked to trust a policy pivot before the activity data confirm it.
PMIs & Activity

The latest factory read was soft: the Caixin PMI showed January activity contracting as Covid lockdowns bit, per Reuters. [[n0146]] That follows a strong 2021 base, with GDP growth of 8.1%, the fastest in a decade, as Global Times reported [[n0130]], and fixed-asset investment up 4.9% in 2021, according to Macau Business. [[n0132]] China Daily reports industrial profits rebounded in 2021 as production improved. [[n0144]] Consumption is the weak leg: CNBC reports the holiday box office plunged 23% as theaters pushed prices to record highs. [[n0171]] On the supply side, Reuters says China plans to increase iron ore output and boost steel-scrap use [[n0024]], a sign Beijing wants to contain input costs for the infrastructure push that China Briefing describes as the growth lever for 2022. [[n0236]]
Credit Impulse

The clearest early win for the easing camp is credit. Reuters reports Chinese government bond yields rose on faster January credit growth [[n0214]], which is the bond market saying it believes the impulse is turning. Lower policy rates reinforce that, with Fibre2Fashion noting cuts to medium-term lending and reverse repo rates. [[n0139]] The mechanism matters for global assets: a rising Chinese credit impulse tends to support Asian cyclicals and industrial commodities with a lag, but this cycle the property sector is where much of the new credit needs to land, and developers' capacity to absorb it is impaired.
Property

Property remains the drag that keeps us from turning Bullish. Reuters reports regulators are giving developers easier access to escrowed presale funds [[n0213]], a targeted liquidity release rather than a bailout. Evergrande says it aims to deliver 600,000 apartments in 2022 with no fire sales, per Reuters [[n0202]], while the WSJ reports its CEO sold bonds before the profit warning [[n0220]], a reminder that bondholder trust is broken. Nikkei Asia's reporting on concrete 'ghost towns' underlines the inventory overhang [[n0201]], and in Hong Kong lived-in home valuations are dropping amid a fifth Covid wave, per the South China Morning Post. [[n0178]] Business Recorder reported in January that new home prices fell less in December on promotions and easing curbs [[n0127]], so price stabilization is being bought with discounts. Escrow relief buys time; it does not create buyers.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade policy is turning more coercive in both directions. China suspended Lithuanian beef, dairy and beer imports as the Taiwan row grows, per Reuters [[n0216]], and Taiwan, Canada and Japan have asked to join the EU's WTO case against China, according to Politico Europe. [[n1457]] The Phase One relationship is souring too: the Peterson Institute calculates China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports in the Trump-era trade deal. [[n0169]] Domestically, oversight keeps tightening, with Reuters reporting a fine for Ant-backed MYBank over credit-scoring rules. [[n0151]] On Russia, The Hill argues China is making sanctions irrelevant [[n1443]], a stance that could raise secondary-sanctions risk for Chinese banks and exporters.
Markets & Flows

Onshore and offshore markets are telling different stories. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,462.95 index points, down 0.66% on Friday and up 3.02% over five sessions, a window that reaches back before the Lunar New Year closure, but still 3.26% lower over 20 sessions; the Hang Seng finished at 24,906.66 index points, 4.92% higher over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). In New York the China A-shares ETF (ASHR) fell 1.93% and the China internet ETF (KWEB) 3.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Regulatory risk remains sharp and idiosyncratic: WuXi Biologics sank by a record after landing on a US red-flag list, per the SCMP. [[n0177]] The SCMP's Macroscope column argues emerging markets are the ones to watch as tech-led US stocks lose their shine. [[n0250]]
New / Most Important

Technology self-sufficiency is the most important new strand. China's biggest chipmaker SMIC posted record revenue despite US sanctions, per CNBC [[n1175]], and plans to boost capacity after doubling profits to US$1.7 billion, according to the SCMP. [[n0243]] At the same time ASML has flagged possible IP infringement by a Chinese 'little giant', per the SCMP [[n0208]], which the Chinese company denies, according to Reuters. [[n0768]] Nikkei Asia reports ZTE is boosting its chip capabilities amid Huawei's crackdown woes. [[n0199]] Foreign capital is still committing to the premium consumer: BMW paid $4.2 billion to take control of its Chinese joint venture, Reuters reports. [[n0763]] Capital is flowing toward strategic self-sufficiency and premium consumption rather than the old property-led model.
Playbook ✓

Action: keep China at neutral, expressed through Hong Kong-listed platforms such as Tencent (453.04 HKD, up 6.84% over 20 sessions) rather than the A-share ETF (ASHR, down 4.07% over 20 sessions) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger to upgrade: a second month of accelerating credit growth alongside a factory PMI back in expansion. What changes the call: new US listing or sanctions actions against Chinese firms, or an escrow scheme that fails to stop developer defaults. ⚠ Divergence: bond yields are rising on faster credit growth, which normally signals reflation, yet the Caixin factory gauge is contracting and holiday spending is weak; the credit impulse has not yet reached activity.

geo.label: BOJ anchored, autos chip-constrained
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is the least exposed major market to the Fed shock through policy, and among the most exposed through industry. The BOJ still applies a negative rate to some bank deposits, including MUFG Bank's, per the Asahi Shimbun [[n1517]], and Reuters reported in January that it was debating how to message an eventual rate hike as inflation perks up. [[n1508]] Tokyo was shut for a holiday on Friday, so the Nikkei 225's last close of 27,696.08 index points, up 0.42%, predates the US risk-off (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). We are Mixed: policy is a cushion, but the export sector is chip-constrained.
Activity & Currency

The industrial picture is a chip story. Toyota's profits fell as production was hit, per the BBC [[n0550]], and the Japan Times argues that after a tough 2021 the outlook for Japanese carmakers is now down to chips. [[n1154]] Nissan raised its profit outlook but sees chips limiting growth, according to Reuters. [[n1086]] Demand is not the constraint: Reuters reported in January that December exports and imports hit record highs by value as supply bottlenecks eased. [[n1510]] Toyota closed at 2,254.00 JPY, down 6.55% over 20 sessions, while chip-equipment makers Tokyo Electron (57,150.00 JPY) and Advantest (9,600.00 JPY) rose 1.82% and 2.78% in their last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). On the currency, the mechanics favor the dollar: with the US two-year at 1.50% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11) and Japanese wages not rising, as the Japan Times explains [[n1531]], rate differentials keep widening, and the DXY is 1.36% firmer over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight Japanese chip-equipment names into the reopening, because the US-listed Japan ETF (EWJ) fell 0.81% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 4.83% in a session Tokyo missed (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger: Tokyo Electron failing to hold its last-session gain would confirm the catch-down. What changes the call: evidence that chip supply is easing for carmakers, or a BOJ signal of normalization that would remove the rate-differential tailwind for exporters.

geo.label: RBA patient as QE ends
parts: Macro Stance

Australia combines strong domestic data with a central bank that wants more proof before hiking. The SMH reports Australia is ending QE with a murky future for $650b of assets [[n0053]], following the RBA's February policy statement. [[n0016]] Inflation hit 3.5%, per the AFR [[n0009]], and the jobless rate is at a 13-year low, per The Australian. [[n0004]] We are Mixed: the data argue for hikes sooner than the RBA signals.
Demand & Financing

Credit demand is still driven by housing. CBA reported a first-half profit surge on the home boom and unveiled a share buyback, per Reuters [[n0033]], and The Australian says the bank is bullish on the economy as rate hikes loom. [[n0512]] The AFR flags rising rents as a sleeper factor for inflation [[n0060]], and the reopening of borders to vaccinated tourists on February 21 adds a services impulse, per Al Jazeera. [[n0022]] Supply remains a bottleneck, with Al Jazeera also reporting that border limbo in the mining state is sparking production fears. [[n0066]] Markets were softer on Friday: the S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.98% to 7,217.30 index points and CBA lost 2.21% to 98.55 AUD, while CSL is down 11.79% over 20 sessions and BHP gained 1.20% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11).
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer the iron ore miners, with Fortescue up 6.98% over five sessions and Rio Tinto up 2.86% on Friday, over the banks while the RBA keeps its patient line (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Trigger: a hawkish shift in RBA language after the next wage or inflation print. What changes the call: China's plan to raise domestic iron ore output, reported by Reuters [[n0024]], turning into weaker seaborne demand, or a faster RBA pivot that slows bank loan growth.

geo.label: NBP hawkish on the front line
parts: Macro Stance

Poland combines the most hawkish central bank in our coverage with the most direct exposure to the Russia–Ukraine risk, which is why we are Mixed rather than outright Bearish. The Monetary Policy Council (RPP) raised rates again, taking them to their highest level in almost nine years, according to Rzeczpospolita. [[n1683]] NBP Governor Adam Glapiński framed his press conference around being a hawk ('Ja jako jastrząb', or 'Me as a hawk'), Interia reported [[n1697]], and Bankier credited him with strengthening the zloty [[n1720]], which it later described as the strongest in eight months. [[n1746]] The inflation problem behind that stance is real: GUS put end-2021 inflation at 8.6%, per 300Gospodarka [[n1595]], and Credit Agricole has raised its 2022 forecast to 7.5%, per Bankier. [[n1598]] The labour market keeps the pressure on, with average pay up 9.6% in 2021, per pb.pl [[n1722]], and registered unemployment at 5.6% in January, per Radio Maryja citing the family and social policy ministry (MRiPS). [[n1615]]
Markets

Warsaw has lagged the hawkish story. The iShares MSCI Poland ETF (EPOL) fell 3.88% on Friday to 20.31 USD and is down 10.96% over 20 sessions, while the WIG20 total-return tracker lost only 0.55% to 37.94 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). The gap reflects mechanics: EPOL trades in dollars during New York hours, so it absorbs both currency translation and late-session US news, whereas the Warsaw close comes earlier in the day. Banks, the natural beneficiaries of higher rates, were heavy: Bank Pekao fell 2.24% to 133.15 PLN and PKO Bank Polski 1.04% to 47.65 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). Parkiet still argues bank shares on the GPW have the potential to extend their bull run [[n1752]], while Bankier asks whether the market is still in a correction or already in a bear market. [[n1738]]
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal numbers are better than feared, but the politics are messier. The finance ministry estimates the 2021 state budget deficit at 26.3 bn zł, per Bankier [[n1776]], and Rzeczpospolita argues inflation is helping the government manage the public debt. [[n1623]] The Polski Ład tax reform has become a liability: deputy finance minister Jan Sarnowski, who was responsible for it, has lost his post, according to Business Insider Polska [[n1775]], a dismissal PolsatNews ties to the problems with Polski Ład [[n1772]], and Wyborcza.biz reports the next finance minister will be a woman. [[n1679]] Spending pressure is building, with pension indexation set to cost more than the budget assumed because of a higher index, per 300Gospodarka. [[n1787]] The food VAT cut is a double-edged tool that Credit Agricole says will contribute to higher inflation, per Bankier. [[n1591]] Relations with Brussels remain strained, with the EU set to withhold funds over the coal mine dispute, per DW. [[n1562]]
Corporate & Sectors

Corporate news is dominated by energy security and state champions. Orlen's CEO says jobs at Lotos will be maintained, per Bankier [[n1682]], and INNPoland reports Orlen has raised its wholesale petrol price, with stations unwilling to absorb the increase. [[n1674]] KGHM has registered its copper cathodes on China's INE exchange, according to Inwestycje.pl [[n1672]], and Parkiet reports Jacek Sasin and KGHM are travelling to the US in pursuit of small nuclear reactors. earnings_pattern.title: Pricing power paid, guidance gaps punished
parts: Rewarded

The market is paying for pricing power and visible cash return. Mercedes-Benz Group jumped 6.72% on Friday to 74.44 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after beating its profit forecast, per Reuters. [[n0797]] GeekWire reports Zillow shares rose 16% on its 'housing super app' strategy amid the iBuying closure [[n0734]], and Reuters says Disney+ streaming growth and park revenue boosted Disney's shares. [[n0532]] Bloom Energy rose 8.97% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after publishing its fourth-quarter results and long-term growth update. [[n0645]]
Punished

Growth stories with soft outlooks are being sold hard. Affirm fell 20.67% to 46.55 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after results that PYMNTS says shine a light on merchant take-rate tradeoffs. [[n0754]] Uber is down 4.75% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) after its 2024 profit forecast fell short of expectations, per Reuters. [[n0717]] CNBC reports Delivery Hero's CEO apologized after a 30% stock plunge [[n0774]], and Reuters says Lyft's weak rider numbers outweighed its first full-year profit. [[n0426]]
Pattern

The common thread is duration. With the two-year up 59 bps in 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-11), investors discount distant profits more heavily and reward companies that can lift prices or shrink their share count now. BP is the template: AJ Bell argues falling debt helps explain its rising share price [[n0779]], and BP rose 1.58% to 417.20 GBp on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11). A beat is not enough when costs threaten margins: Coca-Cola and PepsiCo both warned of an inflation bite, per Reuters [[n0651]], and Coca-Cola fell 1.78% on Friday.
Attention into EPS

Attention now shifts to whether cost inflation reaches margins in the next round of reports. Early reporters are diverging: The Toy Book reports Hasbro revenue spiked 17% in 2021 [[n1050]], Shimano hit record revenue and earnings in its centennial year, per Bicycle Retailer [[n1081]], while Thomson Reuters missed on earnings but set higher revenue goals, according to Reuters. [[n1098]] DuPont's beat on price hikes, per Reuters [[n0404]], is the model the market wants to see repeated.
Playbook

Action: buy results that combine a beat with pricing or buybacks on the first pullback, and fade beats that rely on volume while warning on costs. Trigger: a stock that holds its post-results gain while the VIX stays above 27.36 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-11) has demonstrated real sponsorship. What changes the call: if the two-year stops rising, the punished long-duration names become short-squeeze candidates and the pricing-power premium compresses.
